newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Solana hails improving relations with Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Solana hails improving relations with Ukraine.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, fresh from inconclusive talks on a new post-Cold War relationship with Russia, on Wednesday handed a draft document to Ukraine President Leonid Kuchma outlining a partnership with the former Soviet republic.

"I had the opportunity this morning to hand to President Kuchma the first draft of our document that eventually will be the NATO-Ukraine bilateral relationship," Solana told reporters after meeting the Ukrainian leader.
"I'm sure we will be able to work fast enough so that we can formally sign the document on the occasion of the summit that will take place in Madrid on July 8 and 9," he added.
Ukraine does not share Russia's strong opposition to NATO plans to admit Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic at the July summit.
But like Russia, it is seeking something on paper to fend off any security threat as Europe restructures its defence lines.
Kuchma said his meeting with Solana had been "very fruitful" and added: "There are no contradictions and we have good prospects before us."

Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that Ukraine was not seeking entry to NATO but wanted a concrete mechanism of consultations with its Western partners if security threats arose in the future.
He said he hoped Solana would bring the draft document with him as time was running out before the Madrid summit.
Military analysts in Moscow said Solana's visit to Kiev risked further complicating the task of reaching a deal with Russia to alleviate its fears about NATO expansion.

Ukrainian-Russian relations have been strained since Kiev won independence in 1991 by differences over the former Soviet Black Sea Fleet, based on the Crimean peninsula which is now on independent Ukrainian soil.
The fleet is included in negotiations with Moscow on updating the Conventional Forces in Europe treaty limiting numbers and placement of conventional weapons.
Ukraine has been reluctant to agree to the amended version's signing, expected to take place on May 15, but the fact that Solana brought the draft to Kiev was a sign it had backed down.
Solana met Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov in Luxembourg on Tuesday and though they failed to reach a new deal on relations, both sides said "some progress" had been made.
Primakov said Solana would arrive in Moscow on May 13 for further negotiations.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin's spokesman said after Solana arrived in Kiev that NATO should make more effort to achieve a deal with Russia.
Solana was also in Kiev to open a NATO information centre aimed at calming lingering suspicions among Ukraine's 51 million people of the Western alliance.
Ukraine has played an active role in the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's Partnership for Peace programme and has 500 peacekeeping troops in Bosnia.
It has irritated Yeltsin with plans to host naval exercises with NATO in August off the Crimean peninsula, which is home to a largely ethnic Russian population.
